Gradient Propagation: The `backward()` callback converts output derivatives into input derivatives, and for methods with implicit reads, the system issues atomic scatter-reductions to update scene parameter gradients [S1].

The claim states that the `backward()` callback converts output derivatives into input derivatives. The evidence states: 'When an AD traversal encounters a CustomOp on the tape, it will invoke its forward() or backward() callbacks to convert function input derivatives into output derivatives, or vice versa.' This supports the conversion aspect. The claim also states that for methods with implicit reads, the system issues atomic scatter-reductions to update scene parameter gradients. The evidence explicitly states: 'The reverse mode derivative of a method call with implicit reads will issue atomic scatter-reductions to update scene parameters gradients.' Both parts of the claim are directly supported by the text.
